events.author: Benjamin Gautron
events.name: An Ancient Opponent

options.text: And the [family] have ruled the city wisely ever since.
We will not easily forget this agression!

events.text: We have met the [rival] again. In times long past, their armies sacked [city]... It was at this occasion that the [family] rose to power there.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Anthropology

options.text: We shall study [rival] peacefully.

tip: As leader: +10% Unit Trait Modifier / Siege
As leader: +10% Unit Trait Modifier / Ship

options.text: We shall engage in some practical learning.

events.text: We have made contact with [rival], which could be an excellent learning opportunity for us. They surely have their own culture and knowledge which will be fascinating to learn about. Although, on the other hand, it could also be an interesting exercise to find out exactly how many siege engines it takes to batter down the walls of [city].

events.author: Bob Thomas
events.name: Attacked By a Bear

options.text: Escort the survivors to the nearest settlement.
Provide the survivors with a guide, but send our people on.
Promise to notify the nearest settlement of their plight.

events.text: Two overturned wagons are discovered in a clearing, their goods scattered across the grass. [rival] woman and her children weep over a dead body. The survivors claim that a bear attacked them without warning.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Building Better Relations

options.text: I welcome their admiration.
I welcome their resources!

events.text: We have made contact with [rival], fresh eyes to gaze upon your great works with admiration! And yet, perhaps if we were to seize their resources for ourselves, you could put them to better use?

events.author: Velociryx
events.name: Charm or Malice?

options.text: Smiles, everyone! Smiles! Let us be gracious to our new friends.
This is the perfect opportunity to let my dark side out. Hire bandits to raid their lands, but do it quietly.
Take no special action either way. Let us not show our hand, for the time being.

events.text: Having discovered the nation of [rival] established near us, we are presented with a unique opportunity. We can use the occasion to go out of our way to befriend these people, or we can try and cause them trouble…

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Children of the Nile

options.text: Accept their offerings and match their value with gifts of your own.
Offer to send mercenary fighters as a sign of friendship.
Reply that the lands of [rival] are ours by right. Ready your bows!

events.text: Our scouts have been met by the people of [rival]. Although your ancestors spilled each other's blood across many vicious wars and invasions, these people follow the god Amun, the same one you know as Amani. Warily, they have offered a gift of jewels and incense. How will you treat with these fellow children of the Nile? Are they brothers in arms or bitter rivals?

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Command Decision

options.text: More maneuvers are needed first.
Collect my best maps and fetch my armor, we go to war!

events.text: In meeting [rival] there is the opportunity of leading your army against a new opponent, but some say it might be better to continue to drill for now and attack when better prepared.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Convert or Kill

options.text: We shall give them time to learn.
Why wait? Let us start with the sword!

events.text: We have made contact with [rival]. An ignorant people, they must be brought to know and worship [religion] or be put to the sword!

events.author: Solver
events.name: Debating [rival]

options.text: Let [character] do what she does best.
It is prudent to remain patient and let [rival] show their intentions first.
I will do as [character] suggests.

events.text: A fierce debate arises in the court about how we should treat [rival] whose envoys we just met. [character] urges you to be a despot to them, treating them as beasts to be subjugated. Your mother [character] believes it's better politics to trade with foreigners before killing them and says she can fool [rival] leaders into paying us if you let her lead a delegation to [rival].

events.author: Solver
events.name: Earth and Water

options.text: We do not know how powerful [rival] is - we shall do as they ask.
We are ready to treat with [rival] as equals. If they want our goods, they can come and try get them.
Order their envoys thrown down a well. There they can dig for earth and water for themselves.

events.text: Your patrol comes across men from [rival] and the meeting is immediately tense. The strange [rival] men wear odd clothes and style their beards in a most impractical manner. Could they be skilled soldiers? Are they just another barbarian people? One of the [rival] envoys speaks sufficient Greek to express their demands - 'earth and water'. They desire our submission and tribute but is there any real strength behind their words?

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: First Contact

options.text: Show them our goodwill with a gift.
Keep the meeting civil, but that is all.
We must dominate them.

events.text: We have encountered citizens of the nation of [rival]. While not overtly hostile, these strangers seem wary of our people. How shall we approach the [rival]?

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: First Contact

options.text: Keep the meeting civil, but that is all.
We must crush them!

events.text: We have encountered people from the realm of [rival]. They are led by [character], a <p.is_sub.S0=SUBJECT_ZEALOT>pious fool<p=SUBJECT_SCHOLAR>bookish intellectual<p=SUBJECT_ORATOR>rambling windbag<p=SUBJECT_DIPLOMAT>worm-tongued manipulator<p=SUBJECT_SCHEMER>scheming sneak<p=SUBJECT_HERO>puffed up braggart<p=SUBJECT_TACTICIAN>conceited bore<p=SUBJECT_COMMANDER>military-obsessed fanatic<p=SUBJECT_BUILDER>tinkering obsessive<p=SUBJECT_JUDGE>judgemental type<else>bore with no personality<end> who is likely to <p.is_sub.S0=SUBJECT_ZEALOT>preach unendingly at us<p=SUBJECT_SCHOLAR>bore us with rhetoric<p=SUBJECT_ORATOR>babble on endlessly<p=SUBJECT_DIPLOMAT>attempt to force us into treaties<p=SUBJECT_SCHEMER>constantly meddle in our affairs<p=SUBJECT_HERO>posture threatenly<p=SUBJECT_TACTICIAN>think everything can be solved by one big battle<p=SUBJECT_COMMANDER>march their army around constantly<p=SUBJECT_BUILDER>come begging for resources<p=SUBJECT_JUDGE>condemn our entirely practical actions<else>be disgustingly neutral<end>. How shall we approach the [rival]?

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: First Contact

options.text: Show them our goodwill with a gift.
Keep the meeting civil, but that is all.
We must dominate them.

events.text: We have encountered people from the realm of [rival]. They are led by [character], known as <p.is_sub.S0=SUBJECT_ZEALOT>a Zealot Archetype<p=SUBJECT_SCHOLAR>a Scholar Archetype<p=SUBJECT_ORATOR>an Orator Archetype<p=SUBJECT_DIPLOMAT>a Diplomat Archetype<p=SUBJECT_SCHEMER>a Schemer Archetype<p=SUBJECT_HERO>a Hero Archetype<p=SUBJECT_TACTICIAN>a Tactician Archetype<p=SUBJECT_COMMANDER>a Commander Archetype<p=SUBJECT_BUILDER>a Builder Archetype<p=SUBJECT_JUDGE>a Judge Archetype<else>a leader with no defining trait<end>. How shall we approach the [rival]?

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: First Contact

options.text: I see you are a man of culture as well.
Show them our goodwill with a gift.

events.text: We have encountered people from the realm of [rival]. They are led by [character], a man of such <p.is_sub.S1=SUBJECT_ZEALOT>strong faith<p=SUBJECT_SCHOLAR>great knowledge<p=SUBJECT_ORATOR>cunning words<p=SUBJECT_DIPLOMAT>ability to understand and compromise<p=SUBJECT_SCHEMER>great cunning<p=SUBJECT_HERO>fame<p=SUBJECT_TACTICIAN>battlefield prowess<p=SUBJECT_COMMANDER>strategic genius<p=SUBJECT_BUILDER>creative ability<p=SUBJECT_JUDGE>sound judgement<else>good looks<end> that you cannot help but admire him. How shall we approach the [rival]?

events.author: Bob Thomas
events.name: Friend or Foe?

options.text: Invite the travelers to settle in [rival].
Tell them nothing of us.
Take them captive to learn [rival]'s secrets.

events.text: Our troops encounter a group of traveling artisans. They say that their nation of [rival] has already established a great civilization in distant lands, but they wish to see the world. What shall we tell them?

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Friendly Meeting

options.text: Show them our goodwill with a gift.
Keep the meeting civil, but that is all.
We must dominate them.

events.text: Messengers from the nation of [rival] greet our scouts, inviting them to an informal gathering. These agents of the [rival] court appear pleased to make contact with us, and they encourage warm relations. How shall we respond?

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Glory is Eternal

options.text: In time they will learn.
Then I must teach them!

events.text: We have made contact with [rival]. Initial communication was difficult as it appears they have not heard of you or your great deeds, so our scouts had no common frame of reference.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Happy Days!

options.text: Welcome them as brothers!

events.text: We have made contact with [rival]. An enlightened people, they also worship [religion]. This is most joyous news!

events.author: Bob Thomas
events.name: Hostile Neighbors

options.text: Pay a tribute in gold.
Pay a tribute in iron.
Pay a tribute in food.
Refuse to pay any tributes.
Persuade the soldiers to trade.

events.text: As our units approach the [rival] border, they are met by armed soldiers. These men bring an aggressive message: all nations willing to treat with [rival] must pay tribute. We should be careful how we respond.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Injured [rival]

options.text: Treat his wounds and escort the caravan to its destination.
Negotiate an exchange of protection for goods.
Kill the [rival] and steal their cargo.

events.text: Shouts from the trees! Our men hurry towards the noise and discover an injured [rival] lying in the dirt. His companions work frantically to treat his wounds. According to the men, their caravan was transporting goods to the nearest [rival] city, when they were attacked by bandits. They managed to repel the attackers and save their cargo of fine wine.

events.author: Benjamin Gautron
events.name: Kingmakers in Mesopotamia

options.text: Let them remember: They owe us!
Actually, if they could pay back the favor now...

events.text: We've just made contact with the [rival] again. In times past, a [rival] king sacked [city] and installed the [family] as rulers of their capital and kingdom.

events.author: Benjamin Gautron
events.name: Kingmaking Reversal in Mesopotamia

options.text: I'm sure they'll forgive our intervention, in time...
Let us bring gifts, to salve old grudges.

events.text: We've just made contact with the [rival] again. In times past, a [rival] king sacked [city] and tried to install the [family] as rulers of their capital and kingdom. However the [family] have since been ousted from power and [character] doesn't have very fond memories of our people.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Momentous Meeting

options.text: The scouts will accept this gracious gesture.
[rival] ways are not our ways.

tip: As leader: +10% Unit Trait Modifier / Tribal
As general: +25% Unit Trait Modifier / Tribal

options.text: We will not pretend to respect these [rival].

events.text: A group of curious [rival] appear on the path ahead, as if expecting our men. Removing all weapons, they place them on the ground at their feet. The leader, who speaks our language, expresses excitement over this momentous meeting, offering a gift of fine meat and wine. [rival] means us no harm... or so they say.

events.author: Bob Thomas
events.name: Neighbors

options.text: Humble. We speak little of our own people, asking many questions.
Friendly. We trade news about our people for information about theirs.
Prideful. We boast about our nation's strength, leaving them little chance to speak.

events.text: Your scouts report that they have made contact with a neighboring nation, the [rival]. What is our demeanor as you approach them?

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Plans of Attack

options.text: For now, we wait.
They won’t expect war so soon!

events.text: Now that we have met [rival], an opportunity presents itself. One possibility would be to lure them into a false sense of security by offering to continue the status quo until we are better ready to strike, but another is to simply attack immediately to take them by surprise.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Political Prisoner

options.text: Follow their advice and move along.
Fight them for possession of the prisoner.

requirements.label: Archetype Regal / Archetype Thoughtful
tip: The leader must have one of: Archetype Regal (a character trait); Archetype Thoughtful (a character trait)

options.text: Convince the [rival] to release him into our custody.

events.text: Our scouts encounter a party of [rival] soldiers whipping a man bound by his wrists and ankles. The warriors accuse the man of inciting rebellion, of stalking members of the royal family and attempting to infiltrate the treasury. However, the victim insists that he is innocent of the crimes. The [rival] urge our men to move along and mind their business.

events.author: Solver
events.name: Predestined Enemies?

options.text: We need friends. Offering gifts is prudence, not weakness.
For now, we will go our separate ways. In the future... time will show.
I will not rest until [rival] is destroyed!

events.text: It is with great unease that you hear about our first meeting with [rival]. Even though there is nothing hostile about the encounter, you have a feeling that [rival] cannot be an ally. It is as if Baal Hammon himself is sending images into your mind of their soldiers engaging ours in battle. You're not the only one to feel ill at ease with [rival], but the decision is yours alone - can we ignore the feeling and befriend them? Or is it our destiny to fight these foreigners until only one nation remains standing?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Predestined Enemies?

options.text: The gods will see Rome to victory.
We will wait to see how this unfolds.
We should be seeking allies, not enemies.

events.text: Our scouts bring word of a newly contacted nation: [rival]. From the accounts of their people, this is a highly sophisticated and cultured empire, with the military might to match. A chill grips you. Although Rome has expanded under your rule, there is something that tells you that this encounter will be unlike any that you have faced so far. The people of Rome are wary that [rival] may try to curb your expansion, but ultimately the decision falls to you. How will you treat this rival nation?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Priest of a Foreign Land

options.text: Invite them to your court to learn more of [religion].
Keep a wary distance.

tip: As leader: -40 Opinion with all Religions

options.text: We will burn their gods to the ground.

events.text: Your people have met a group of traveling [religion] priests from the land of [rival]. They say that their people are a devoted nation, eager to make allies with fellow followers of. How will you treat these [rival]?

events.name: Priest of a Foreign Land

Keep a wary distance.

Keep a wary distance.

Keep a wary distance.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Sharing Spirits

options.text: We shall give them time to learn.
Why wait? Let us start with the sword!

events.text: We have made contact with [rival]. An ignorant people, they must be brought to know and worship the same spirits which guide us or be put to the sword!

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Stirring Speech

options.text: I shall make a plea for peace!
Sometimes patience is the best course of action.
I shall fan the flames of war!

events.text: We have made contact with [rival], so of course this must be the focus of today’s speech. But shall you focus on welcoming a new friend, or will you stir your people to war?

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Stories and Souvenirs

options.text: Show them our goodwill with a gift.
Keep the meeting civil, but that is all.
We must dominate them.

events.text: Scouts encounter an expedition of strangers following a similar route. They call themselves [rival] and hail from a distant land beyond the horizon. Sharing a cordial meal, the two groups exchange stories and souvenirs. How shall our scouts conclude this meeting?

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Tactical Analysis

options.text: A swift strike is better!

events.text: After encountering [rival] you have two main tactical options, either to wait and gather more information, or to launch an immediate attack!

events.author: nolegskitten
events.name: The Continuation of Policy

options.text: They should consider themselves lucky. In truth, we're doing them a favor.

events.text: You have just met emissaries from [rival]. Using a skillfully crafted mix of veiled threat, sugary diplomacy, and erudite readings of ancient pledges of support and allegiance, you manage to convince them that a tribute is rightfully due!

events.author: nolegskitten
events.name: The Continuation of Policy

outcomes.label: Assyria Ashur Uballit I The Continuation Of Policy Wood
Assyria Ashur Uballit I The Continuation Of Policy Iron
Assyria Ashur Uballit I The Continuation Of Policy Food
Assyria Ashur Uballit I The Continuation Of Policy Stone

events.text: You have just met emissaries from [rival]. Using a skillfully crafted mix of veiled threat, sugary diplomacy, and erudite readings of ancient pledges of support and allegiance, you manage to convince them that a tribute is rightfully due!

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: The Fool

options.text: Bring Pieface to the palace for our amusement.
I have no interest in the follies of a fool.
His skills are best put to use in the fields.
He will be my private tutor in the art of jest.

events.text: On a hilltop, dressed in a patchwork of rags and stockings, stands a curious figure calling himself Pieface. This self-proclaimed "fool, buffoon, and bungler" hails from the distant nation of [rival], which he recently departed in search of work abroad. Our scouts seem unsure about this unusual character, though they find his escapades delightful.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Treaty Time

options.text: There must be peace in our time.
Keep the meeting civil, but that is all.
We shall continue diplomacy by other means!

events.text: The recent encounter with [rival] means that we must formalize our relationship with a treaty! Should we make a non-binding pact of neutrality, or present a formal declaration of war?

events.author: Soren Johnson
events.name: Tutorial: Nation Contact

options.text: I'll do my best to make some friends!

events.text: You've encountered a rival nation! Rival nations are your primary opponents in Old World. You may engage them diplomatically, which could lead to gaining a powerful trade partner and ally, or declare War on them to conquer their territory. You decide which nations are worthy of being your allies and which should simply be conquered. At some difficulty levels, other nations begin the game already established with a number of Cities, Units, and Improvements. If you hover the mouse over [rival]'s name in the leaderboard at the top left of screen, you can find out important information about them, such as the number of Cities they have, how strong their Military is, how developed they are technologically, and also with whom they are currently at War or Peace. To conduct diplomacy, you must appoint an Ambassador (requires Aristocracy).

events.author: Bob Thomas
events.name: Unknown Nation

options.text: Avoid them, as we have enemies enough.
Interact with them, and share freely.

events.text: Our scouts have encountered travelers from a foreign land. Although they speak a strange tongue, these men and women appear harmless. They wish to greet our people and establish relations. Do we dare risk our nation's security?

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Value Judgement

options.text: Who am I to Judge them?
I condemn them. The penalty is death!

events.text: Reports are beginning to arrive about the society of [rival] after our recent encounter. They seem to have very different morals and standards from us, and do not uphold the same values at all.
